Module open · 5/5 · the next 4:00 — Unit 480 · power generation · 55 slides · 240 min

What Module 109 covers

One area, and it is the power plant of the plant: everything you have learnt in the previous modules runs on what comes out of here. Seven gas gensets, two diesel gensets, four busbars at 690 V and a master that decides how many machines run — in permanent island mode.

  • Start with the numbers — what the plant asks for and what is installed: five running, two in reserve.
  • Follow the fuel gas on one drawing: two headers, not one, and fourteen orifice plates.
  • Open the machine. A lean-burn engine with a prechamber, its gas train, its water, its oil, its batteries.
  • Then safety — gas and fire in a closed container, and the cause-and-effect matrix.
  • Finish in the control room: what the PCS can and cannot do, black start, and the four screens.

▶ IN · across the fence2 streams + the commands
HP fuel gas from Unit 370stream F36 off the vaporiser, warmed in X-373 — a 3 kW electric heater, not a hot-oil one — before it enters the distribution header. This is what the seven gas engines burn.
Diesel, by roadinto TK-481, lifted by P-481A/B, the power generator diesel pumps, on line GO-480001 to the two diesel sets — the fuel that does not depend on the plant running
And the commandsthe plant safety system reaches in: 50 PSD causes trip all seven gas sets, and ESD levels 1 to 5 trip the gas sets and start the two diesels

Block 1 · before any operating detail — Area 480 · gas engine modules in sealed containers · 690 V generation

The hazards of this unit

One module, six distinct risks: the gas it burns, the voltage it makes, the heat and the noise of its exhaust, the air inside the container, and what turns or burns while it runs.

1 · gas in a closed container
1–8 BARG
  • Gas train inside a sealed container — a leak fills the enclosed air
  • 20% LEL → prealarm + module stop · 40% LEL → alarm
  • Gas + fire together: gas wins — ventilate before smothering
2 · electrical
690 V · 85 kA
  • Four 690 V TN-C busbars, breaking capacity Icu 85 kA
  • Breaker +GENCB 2,500 A — only the engine control closes it
  • 24 V AGM batteries also feed the Master Control, diode-decoupled
3 · exhaust heat
385 °C
  • 10,118 kg/h of exhaust gas through a DN600 duct
  • Uninsulated sections: contact and radiant burns
  • A stopped engine is not a cold duct — heat stays after the stop
4 · noise
106 dBA
  • Dry cooler fans 11-AER-1 rated LWA 106 dBA
  • Silencer 13-SIL-1 takes the exhaust down to 72 dB(A)
  • Hearing protection near the container and the cooler
5 · CO & confined space
GAS-TIGHT BOX
  • The module container is a sealed, gas-tight enclosure
  • Purge fan + damper run after every stop and every failed start
  • Never re-enter without a verified gas-clear condition
6 · rotating parts, fuel & LOTO
1,500 RPM
  • Engine and alternator turn at 1,500 rpm — nothing is reached into
  • Diesel day tank 1,000 L over a containment bund
  • Lock-out / tag-out before any intervention
the area answersGD ×11gas detectionFD ×2flame detectionSD ×6smoke detectionHS-480-ES6ESD pushbuttonXL-480-ES6ESD beacon
Never re-enter a module container without a verified gas-clear condition, and never open a panel or reach into the machine without lock‑out / tag‑out.purge fan runs after every stop and every failed start · LOTO per TA 2300-0010
Which detector trips what is not printed here — the strip lists what is installed (plant instrument registry, unit 480); the cause-and-effect is SAF12-ING-FR01. Figures on the cards are the project record of the module: TSOC Sec.6.8, PLANT_ARCHITECTURE, PID-00, CLARKE_F4, CLARKE_F6_DIESEL and TA 2300-0010.

The fuel gas path, end to end

║ FE orifice plate: FE-4801…4807 Ø30 mm on the seven 3" branches, FE-4811…4817 Ø5 mm on the seven 1" branches. The fourteen FT-48xx, plus PT/TT-4801 and PT/TT-4810, are what the PCS reads (DB101).Amber is safety: PSV-4801A/B relieve the 1" line at 10 barg to the hot flare. Block 3 · the engine — JMS 612 GS-N.L · 12 cyl V · 2 turbos · load 50–100% auto / 40–100% island

The engine: J612 lean-burn with prechamber

SYSTEM BLOCK DIAGRAM sheet A, gas-engine zone · lit: turbo · cylinders · TecJet · ignition
gasairwateroilexhaust690 V powersignal
how it worksTwelve cylinders in a V, fed by two turbochargers. The TecJet doses gas on CAN; the LEANOX loop sets that mixture by load and charge temperature, then ignition fires it across all twelve cylinders through the prechamber.

The verified sequence belongs to AC pump M.03-M-002: ≥1 min pre-lube, off above 800 rpm, then 1,5 min post-lube. The source locates the two DC pumps but does not state their operating duty.
1

Past 800 rpm the AC pump stops; the verified source does not identify the circulation path that carries the run from there.

4

On any stop, the AC pump restarts for 1,5 minutes of post-lubrication before it shuts down for good.

Two DC pumps are installed separately: M.03-M-003 in cabinet +V1 and M.03-M-004 in cabinet +EV1.

Block 3 · starting and stopping — JMS 612 GS-N.L · batteries · master control power · purge · ventilation gating

Starting and stopping the module

Start sequence top, stop sequence below — batteries · starters · engine · +GENCB, then breaker · cooldown · stop · purge
how it worksTwo starter motors turn the engine over on 24 V DC drawn from the module batteries. The same batteries, diode-decoupled, also back the Master Control command power. Room ventilation only runs with the louvers open, room ≥28°C, and no gas alarm present.

Two starter motors, 24 V DCE.00-M-001[01][02] · GENSET_MACHINE_ANATOMY.md:365-374

The module batteries also feed the Master Control command power, decoupled by diodesGENSET_MACHINE_ANATOMY.md:370-374 · SYSTEM_BLOCK_DIAGRAM.md:49-51

Normal stop: once the generator breaker opens, the module keeps running 180 s before it actually stopsCLARKE_F7_OPERATION.md:281-296

Block 3 · air, exhaust, room — combustion air · room ventilation · exhaust · silencer · container

Air, exhaust and the room

Air and exhaust path, louvre to stack — numbers key into the callouts on the right
how it worksTwo separate paths share the room: combustion air goes straight into the engine, while room fans 11-VEN-1/2/3 keep the module itself fit to work in — neither one runs unless the louvres are open, the room is at or above 28°C, and there is no gas alarm. On the way out, the exhaust carries its own heat through the silencer before the P.02-TI-047 signal is read after the catalyst — a temperature, not a piece of equipment.

Block 4 · gas and fire detection — Area 480 · module container · P.17 loop

Gas and fire inside the container

Three sensor types watch the container air: gas, smoke and temperature, each with its own trip and its own scope — and one rule that decides which one wins if both fire.

Gas — P.17-JI-100/101→this module→module shutdown
Smoke — P.17-JI-210/211/212→whole installation→emergency shutdown
Temperature — P.17-TI-010, 50°C→this module→module shutdown
Card colour: red module-only trip / gas priority — amber whole-installation trip — blue interlock / enable condition — plain summary.
Gas detection — dual LEL
20% / 40% LEL
  • Two detectors, P.17-JI-100 / JI-101
  • Thresholds at 20% and 40% LEL, either trips a module shutdown
  • Which threshold drives which action: read off the C&E chart, not this card
Smoke / fire detection
  • Three detectors, P.17-JI-210 / 211 / 212
  • Trip: emergency shutdown of the whole installation
  • Louvers close, ventilation fans stop
Temperature trip
50°C
  • Container temperature, P.17-TI-010
  • At 50°C the module shuts down
  • Same scope as the gas trip — this module only
Ventilation lockout
  • Fan P.17-M-200 needs louvers open, room ≥ 28°C
  • A gas alarm blocks the enable — no added airflow into a leak
  • Same three conditions gate every run, not just the first start
Scope: module vs. whole plant
  • Gas trip (JI-100/101) and heat trip (TI-010): this module stops
  • Smoke trip (JI-210/211/212): the entire installation stops
  • Smoke is read as the more severe event
Gas beats fire
GAS WINS
  • Gas and fire alarm together: gas takes priority
  • Ventilate first — do not smother while gas is present
  • Same priority already set for the whole module (hazards slide)
Sources: TSOC Sec.6.8.2, GENSET_MACHINE_ANATOMY.md (module container detection, :378–389 and :380 for the fan interlock), TA 1504-0400 and TA 1530-0176.

alarms · block 4 — INNIO priority classes — count and action

Four alarm priorities, four actions

Every alarm the gas engine controller can raise falls into one of four INNIO priority classes. The class sets the response — the operator does not choose it.

P19
Emergency stop, immediate trip
Ignition off, generator breaker open, solenoid valves closed — no load reduction step first.
P265
Valves closed, breaker open
Gas valves closed and the generator breaker opened, both in ≤ 1 s.
P327
Normal stop, with cooldown
Controlled shutdown that runs the module through its post-cooling (cooldown) cycle.
P4192
Warning
Signalled to the operator; the module keeps running, no automatic action.
Severity ladder — P1 highest, P4 lowest, bar length = alarm count

P2■ TRIPValves closed, breaker open65
P3▼ COOLNormal stop, with cooldown27
P4● WARNWarning192

BLOCK 5 · AREA 480 — who commands what, and over which cable

The control architecture

PROFIBUS DPtype A, Sub-D 9, RS-485PROFINET IOcat.5e RJ45Modbus TCPcat.5e RJ45, read-onlyHard-wired SSLcopper signal cores4–16 mA load shareanalogue, machine to machineVendor EthernetmyPlant, outbound only
Nine machines, three levels: the module keeps itself alive, +ST1 / +ST2 synchronise and sequence, the PCS asks and commands — but only over copper. PROFIBUS DP is two segments, 14 slaves, 2 per gas module. Sources: PROFIBUS rev 01 issue A3 (design, not yet in service) · SSL-SO59108_BL63 rev C · SYSTEM_BLOCK_DIAGRAM sheet B · plant_power_meters.
BLOCK 5 · AREA 480 — the same sheet, narrowed

Where this sits on the sheet

The nine hard-wired drops (graphite) run from every machine to its master, and on to the PCS card in red. Everything the PCS commands travels on one of those nine SSL numbers — no other copper run leaves the PCS panel. Reads (PROFIBUS, Modbus, the two diesel status) travel a completely different set of wires, shown in full on s41, and none of them lets the PCS write anything back.

The master's automatic mode

One master, one busbar: +ST1 for sections A–B, +ST2 is the corresponding C–D master. The source details +ST1's five modes and timed sequence to add or drop a module.
Modes

Load steps
Load stepPower per half-busbar
Step 11,808 kW

Step 35,424 kW
Sequence
1

Automatic mode picks the mode the flow calls for, then starts the available module with the fewest running hours to cover it.

2

Load transfers onto the module coming in — 5 minutes.

3

Coupling breaker T2 opens — 5 minutes.

4

The module going out of service stops 180 s after its own breaker opens.

In manual mode neither master runs this logic — only load shedding still works. The combination of modules in service is always the operator's choice (plant manual §2.5).

BLOCK 5 · AREA 480 — what the PCS reads today, not what it will read

The PCS screens for Unit 480 — what it reads today

SCREEN MAP (s7_addresses_PCS.csv · PROFIBUS_REV01 issued for approval)
What the operator sees on this PCS page
  1. 19 analogue tags, DB101 AI_Raw — PT/TT-4801, PT/TT-4810, LT-4813, FT-4801..4807 and FT-4811..4817, one header/branch pair per genset run.
  2. 16 ESD bits, STW01_GENERAL — ASD, gas/fire/NH3 alarms, loss-of-signal groups, valve and level trips, read from the safety PLC.
  3. No genset group tag today — power, run status and INNIO alarms per module are not on this PCS page.
  4. That detail is PROFIBUS_REV01 — issued for approval, not yet executed; it will add the group data, not replace the 19 tags above.
  5. Power metering runs separately — the 11 power meters go by Modbus TCP straight to the historian, not through this PCS page.
  6. Today is a subset, not the design limit — by-bus design context is ~45 analogue values + ~28 bits + 191 alarms, read-only; this map shows only what s7_addresses_PCS.csv confirms is wired in today.
BLOCK 5 · AREA 480 — screen map · layout, not live data

ElectricPlantView — the unifilar with nine generators, live

SCREEN MAP (eni/ga-elec.html · ELEC_FUNCTIONAL_GA_PLAN.md)
What the operator reads on this page
  1. Minimum load 50% automatic / 40% island — the floor the automatic sequencer and the isolated-island mode allow; the 30% figure seen elsewhere is not printed here.
  2. Load sharing: 4–16 mA analog loop, 0–100% Pn — a hard-wired current loop shared by all nine machines, not PROFIBUS and not the PCS.
  3. Voltage droop 3% — reactive power splits by voltage statism, identical on all nine gensets.
  4. 11 meters: 9 Modbus / 2 no comms — five on 480-JG-691, four on 480-JG-692; LV-board meters 480-JG-693/694 have no protocol or address populated.
  5. Values remain placeholders — kW, energy and hours show a dash until pulled live at the plant clock.

take-home · recap — eleven key messages · Module 109

Key messages — Module 109

  1. 19 100 kW at 100 %, 12 761 kW installed— 5 modules running, 2 in reserve.
  2. 2Two gases, not one— 1–3 barg to the main train, 4,25–8 barg to the pre-chamber.
  3. 3Methane number 83, minimum 75— below that the engine knocks.
  4. 4Never more than 4 gas modules on one section— the busbar section rating is 85 kA.
  5. 5The coupler always closes onto a dead bus— never onto a live one.
  6. 6PSD/ESD stops all 7 gas modules and starts the 2 diesels— in black start the diesel is step 1.
  7. 7TALL-48xx trips only its own module— any plant-wide PSD trips all seven.
  8. 8The module's batteries also feed the master— one battery bank, two loads.
  9. 9Major overhaul at 60 000 h or 24 000 starts— whichever comes first.
  10. 10“K” is not “the customer does it”— 102 of 171 maintenance tasks are INNIO-only.
  11. 11Gas and fire together — gas wins— the gas-detection priority overrides the fire logic.
